clue.text: Abdicate, putting son in to rule

indicators.note: putting one thing in another means the son's letter goes inside the word for rule

parts.note: to rule is to reign

explanation.surface: A monarch steps down while installing a son on the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne or office formally, to step down from it.

clue.text: Style of architecture in Morocco executed slightly differently

indicators.note: arranged in another way, so the remaining letters are rearranged
an executed person loses the head, so the first letter of the country is cut off

explanation.surface: A building style in North Africa is carried out with small variations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' looks like 'carried out' but means beheaded: MOROCCO loses M, leaving OROCCO, which 'slightly differently' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornate eighteenth-century decorative style of curves and scrollwork in buildings and furnishings.

clue.text: Throw out pitcher — it can be used for pigs

definitions.text: it can be used for pigs

parts.note: to scrap something is to throw it out
an iron is a golf club, one used to pitch the ball

explanation.surface: Discard the jug; it's fine for feeding swine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitcher' looks like a jug and 'pigs' like animals; pigs are cast bars of metal, made from melted-down waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded metal is remelted and cast into pig bars, crude ingots from a furnace.

clue.text: Let off punishment, being emaciated

indicators.note: off means removed, so the word let is taken away from the punishment

parts.note: running the gauntlet was a punishment of being beaten between two lines of men
taken as written

explanation.surface: A culprit is spared a penalty, looking very thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean painfully thin and haggard, as through hunger or illness.

clue.text: Lacking room for expansion, like a lady's slipper, perhaps

definitions.meaning: said of a plant whose roots have filled its container and can grow no further
the lady's slipper is an orchid, often grown in a container, here imagined with roots cramped

explanation.surface: A cramped space is compared to a woman's tight shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: The lady's slipper looks like footwear but is an orchid, a plant whose roots can outgrow its container.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant whose roots have filled the container has no space left to grow.

clue.text: Attack from the kick-off

definitions.meaning: an assault or charge against an enemy
from the start, as in from the beginning of a match

explanation.surface: An offensive is launched as soon as the match starts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an assault and the beginning of something.

clue.text: Hesitation among author's readers using library

indicators.note: placed among means put inside, so the hesitation goes inside the author's name

parts.note: George Borrow was a nineteenth-century English author; with the possessive his name gives BORROWS
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An author's fans pause uncertainly while using the library.
explanation.definitionFit: Library users take books out on loan, so they are lenders' customers who take items temporarily.

clue.text: Unit left, having been mauled throughout the period before

indicators.note: mauled means roughly handled, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An army unit pulled out after a battering lasting the whole time.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means up to the time when, covering all of the time leading up to an event.

clue.text: Jam reported in part of the entrance

definitions.meaning: a word sounding like jam is jamb, the upright side of a door frame
an upright on one side of a doorway

explanation.surface: Something gets stuck, so they say, in the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' suggests a blockage or fruit preserve, but 'reported' turns it into its sound-alike jamb, a side of a door frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the vertical side piece of a door frame, one of its uprights.

clue.text: Vigorous radical said to be erudite

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: well means healthy and vigorous, and red means radical or left-wing

explanation.surface: A firebrand activist is reportedly highly learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has studied many books is learned and scholarly.

clue.text: Baggage handlers have binges, imbibing litres

indicators.note: drinking in, so the binges word takes the litres letter inside it

parts.note: to carouse is to drink and make merry, so carouses are binges

explanation.surface: Airport porters go on drinking sprees, downing litres of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baggage handlers' suggests porters, but it means the moving belts at an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Airport carousels are the rotating belts that deliver luggage to arriving passengers.

clue.text: Prince's friend disposing of house to relation

indicators.note: getting rid of, so the abbreviation for house is taken out of the friend's name

parts.note: Horatio is the friend of Prince Hamlet in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A royal companion sells his home to a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion between two quantities is a mathematical relation between them.

clue.text: Any part of IOU, for example, could be financial asset

definitions.text: Any part of IOU, for example
definitions.meaning: each letter of the abbreviation IOU is an upper-case letter
money or property used to fund a business or investment

explanation.surface: Even a promissory note might count as something of value.
explanation.walkthrough: IOU, a written promise to repay, steers towards money, but the first sense is typographic: its letters are upper-case.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper-case letters are called this; in finance it means wealth invested in an enterprise.

clue.text: Cover protecting bread and tart

indicators.note: the cover word wraps around the bread word, shielding it on both sides

parts.note: a top is a cover or lid
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A lid keeps a loaf and a pastry fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' reads as a pastry beside bread, but it is the slang insult for a promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old disparaging terms for a woman thought sexually loose or slovenly.

clue.text: Border area round NE is suitable for company cars, say

parts.note: a fringe is the outer edge or border region of something

indicators.note: going round means the words for is suitable surround the compass letters

parts.note: befits means is suitable or proper for
NE is north-east, taken as written

explanation.surface: Somewhere on the margins of the north-east is fine for a fleet of company vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Perks such as a car provided by an employer are extras given on top of salary.

clue.text: Something new said to dispel endless gloominess

indicators.note: to dispel is to scatter, so the letters are scattered into a new order
without its end, so the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A fresh remark breaks a long spell of low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last S of GLOOMINESS, and 'dispel' rearranges the remaining GLOOMINES.
explanation.definitionFit: A coined word or phrase, a fresh addition to the language.

clue.text: One who will dispose of anything you have left

definitions.text: One who will dispose of anything you have left

parts.words: One who will dispose of anything you have left
parts.note: reads like a refuse collector or someone clearing junk, but means the person who distributes a dead person's estate

explanation.surface: Someone who will get rid of whatever you leave behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The person named in a will to carry out its terms and distribute the estate.

clue.text: Signora must take both wings off goose

indicators.note: the wings are the two ends, so the first and last letters of the phrase are removed and the inner run remains

explanation.surface: An Italian lady must clip a goose's wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take both wings off' strips S and T from the ends of SIGNORAMUST. 'goose' means a silly person, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a foolish, ignorant person.

clue.text: Trading in. South London area

parts.note: Wapping is a district of East London on the Thames

explanation.surface: Doing business in a district of south London.
explanation.walkthrough: WAPPING is a riverside district of East London, once home to newspaper presses.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchanging one thing for another is trading.

clue.text: Light clothing creating favourable impression

parts.note: a window is a light, letting light into a room
dressing is putting clothes on

explanation.surface: Wearing flimsy garments makes a good first impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy presentation meant to make something look better than it is, like a shop display.

clue.text: Sort of lizard making sudden dart, swallowing nothing

indicators.note: taking in, so the lunge word holds the letter for nothing inside

parts.note: a lunge is a sudden forward thrust
O is the zero shape for nothing

explanation.surface: A reptile darts forward and swallows nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A lounge lizard is not a reptile but an idle man who loiters in bars and smart rooms seeking company.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase lounge lizard names a type of idle, smooth socialiser; the word completes that kind.

clue.text: Play for each class

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A drama staged for every class in the school.
explanation.walkthrough: FORM for a school class is British usage: a year group or class in a school.
explanation.definitionFit: To play music or a role is to act it out or render it before an audience.

clue.text: European citizen runs Arab country

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: A European national manages a Gulf state.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or inhabitant of Rome, an Italian city, is a European citizen.

clue.text: Listlessly moved cycle

explanation.surface: Someone drifted about lethargically on a bike.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of sulk about aimlessly; also a small low-powered motorbike.

clue.text: Work unit in open stand

indicators.note: the unit of work is placed in the word for open

parts.note: to undo is to open or unfasten
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A labour unit takes an open stance.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to endure or put up with it, to go through it.

clue.text: Stalk game, out of sight

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or stalk them
go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A hunter tracks quarry while staying hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: To lie doggo is informal British for staying hidden and keeping still.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang word means hidden, keeping quiet and unseen, as in lie low.

clue.text: A doctor injected into two feet

indicators.note: an injection goes inside, so the letters go into the middle of the Roman two

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic gives a jab into both of someone's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' are metrical units of verse, not body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Metrical units of one short and one long syllable, the plural of the classic verse unit.

clue.text: Controller of stocks and shares given special lunch

definitions.meaning: the stocks and shares are parts of a farm implement, the handles and blades, steered by a farmhand
a cold meal of bread, cheese and pickle served in British pubs

explanation.surface: A stockbroker is treated to a fancy lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial surface misleads: stocks and shares here are parts of a plough. The pub lunch is a British staple of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm worker who drives the plough; his name also labels the pub meal of bread and cheese.

clue.text: Cupholder's variation .. in endgame smothering unknown

indicators.note: covering over, so the rearranged letters surround the unknown
a variation is a changed version, so the letters of endgame are rearranged

parts.note: Y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A chess variation in the endgame smothers an unknown piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' rearranges ENDGAME into GANMEDE, which 'smothering' wraps round Y. The doubled dot is a print artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Trojan youth carried off to Olympus served as cup-bearer to Zeus.

clue.text: Cook us some dessert

indicators.note: to cook can mean to falsify or rework, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Prepare a pudding for the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, airy sweet dish made with whipped cream or egg whites.
